title.zh: 卷一百〇九 漢書11: 列傳六 杜重威 李守貞 趙思綰
title.en: Volume 109 Book of Later Jin 11: Biographies 6 - Du Zhongwei, Li Shouzhen, Zhao Siwan
title.raw: 卷一百〇九 漢書11: 列傳六 杜重威 李守貞 趙思綰 Volume 109 Book of Later Jin 11: Biographies 6 - Du Zhongwei, Li Shouzhen, Zhao Siwan

sentences.zh: 杜重威，其先朔州人，近世徙家於太原。

translations.literal: Du Zhongwei: his ancestors were men of Shuozhou; in recent generations the family moved and settled at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhongwei's forebears were from Shuozhou; in recent generations his family had moved to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖興，振武牙將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xing was a military adjutant of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xing had been a military adjutant in the Zhenwu command.

sentences.zh: 父堆金，事唐武皇為先鋒使。

translations.literal: His father Duijin served Tang's Emperor Wu as vanguard commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duijin had served Emperor Wu of Tang as vanguard commissioner.

sentences.zh: 重威少事明宗，自護聖軍校領防州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongwei in his youth served Emperor Mingzong; from an officer of the Husheng Army he came to hold the post of prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Zhongwei served Emperor Mingzong, rising from an officer in the Husheng Army to prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其妻即晉高祖妹也，累封宋國大長公主。

translations.literal: His wife was a younger sister of the Jin Gaozu; she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a younger sister of Gaozu of Later Jin and was eventually ennobled as Grand Princess of Song.

sentences.zh: 天福初，命重威典禁軍，遙授舒州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Zhongwei was ordered to take charge of the palace guard and was appointed in absentia prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu era he was placed in command of the palace guard and given the nominal post of prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，張從賓構亂，據汜水，晉高祖遣重威與候益率眾破之，以功授潞州節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zhang Congbin raised rebellion and seized Sishui; the Jin Gaozu sent Zhongwei and Hou Yi to lead troops and defeat him, and for this merit Zhongwei was made military governor of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhang Congbin rebelled and held Sishui. Gaozu sent Zhongwei and Hou Yi to crush him, and Zhongwei was made military governor of Luzhou for his service.

sentences.zh: 與楊光遠降範延光於鄴城，改許州節度使，兼侍衛親軍馬步軍副指揮使，尋加同平章事。

translations.literal: Together with Yang Guangyuan he compelled Fan Yanguang to surrender at Yecheng; he was changed to military governor of Xuzhou, and concurrently made deputy commander of the palace guard horse-and-foot armies; shortly he was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: With Yang Guangyuan he forced Fan Yanguang to surrender at Yecheng. He was transferred to Xuzhou as military governor, made deputy commander of the palace guard, and soon elevated to Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移鎮鄆州，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Before long he was shifted to garrison Yanzhou and promoted to commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse-and-foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned to Yanzhou and promoted to commander-in-chief of the palace guard.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：馮道、李崧屢薦重威之能，以為都指揮使，充隨駕御營使。）〉

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian says: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly recommended Zhongwei's ability, making him commander-in-chief and appointing him commissioner of the imperial escort camp.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly praised Zhongwei's talents, secured his appointment as commander-in-chief, and made him commissioner of the imperial escort camp.)

sentences.zh: 及鎮州安重榮稱兵向闕，命重威禦之，敗重榮於宗城。

translations.literal: When An Chongrong of Zhenzhou raised troops and marched on the capital, Zhongwei was ordered to oppose him and defeated Chongrong at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chongrong of Zhenzhou marched on the capital, Zhongwei was sent against him and defeated him at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 重榮奔據常山，重威尋拔其城，斬重榮首傳於闕下，授成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: Chongrong fled and held Changshan; Zhongwei soon took the city, beheaded Chongrong and sent his head to the court, and was appointed military governor of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong fled to Changshan. Zhongwei soon took the city, sent Chongrong's head to the capital, and was made military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 所得重榮家財及常山公帑，悉歸於己，晉高祖知而不問。

translations.literal: The property taken from Chongrong's household and the public funds of Changshan he kept entirely for himself; the Jin Gaozu knew but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He kept for himself all of Chongrong's family wealth and the public treasury of Changshan. Gaozu knew but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，復重斂於民，稅外加賦，境內苦之

translations.literal: On reaching his post he again levied heavily on the people, imposing surcharges beyond the regular taxes, and those within his circuit suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he taxed the people heavily again, piling surcharges on top of regular levies until the whole circuit groaned under him.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：重威所至黷貨，民多逃亡，嘗出過市，謂左右曰：「人言我驅盡百姓，何市人之多也！」）〉

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian says: Wherever Zhongwei went he was corrupt in taking goods; many of the people fled. Once when he went out and passed through the market he said to those at his side: "People say I have driven away all the commoners—why are there so many people in the market!")
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian says that wherever Zhongwei served he plundered the people until many fled. Once, passing through the market, he told his attendants, "They say I have driven every commoner away—then why is the market so crowded?")

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，與契丹絕好，契丹主連年伐晉，重威但閉壁自守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded to the throne, relations with the Khitan were broken off; the Khitan ruler attacked Jin year after year, and Zhongwei only shut his walls and held himself in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shaodi came to the throne, ties with the Khitan were severed. The Khitan khan invaded Jin year after year, and Zhongwei only shut his gates and held his walls.

sentences.zh: 部內城邑相繼破陷，一境生靈受屠戮，重威任居方面，未嘗以一土一騎救之。

translations.literal: Cities and towns within his jurisdiction fell one after another; living beings throughout the circuit were slaughtered, yet Zhongwei, holding a frontier command, never once sent a foot of territory or a single horse to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Town after town in his circuit fell, and the people were slaughtered, yet Zhongwei, though he held a frontier command, never sent a single soldier to their aid.

sentences.zh: 每敵騎數十驅漢人千萬過城下，如入無人之境，重威但登陴註目，略無邀取之意。

translations.literal: Whenever several dozen enemy horsemen drove tens of thousands of Han people past below the walls, as if entering a land with no one in it, Zhongwei only mounted the battlements and watched, with not the slightest intent to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a few dozen enemy horsemen drove thousands of Han captives past his walls as if the land were empty, Zhongwei only climbed the ramparts to watch and never made the least move to stop them.

sentences.zh: 開運元年秋，加北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Kaiyun he was given the additional post of northern campaign commissioner for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first Kaiyun year he was made northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，領大軍下新州、滿城、遂城。

translations.literal: In the second year he led a great army south against Xinzhou, Mancheng, and Suicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he led a great army against Xinzhou, Mancheng, and Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 契丹主自古北口回軍，追躡王師，重威等狼狽而旋，至陽城，為契丹所困。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler turned his army back from Gubeikou and pursued the imperial forces; Zhongwei and the others withdrew in disorder, and when they reached Yangcheng they were beset by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan turned back through Gubeikou and pursued the imperial army. Zhongwei and his men retreated in disorder and, reaching Yangcheng, were trapped by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 會大風狂猛，軍情憤激，府彥卿、張彥澤等引軍四出，敵眾大潰，諸將欲追之，重威曰：「逢賊得命，更望復子乎！

translations.literal: It happened that a fierce wind blew; the army's spirit was roused to anger; Fu Yanqing, Zhang Yanze, and others led troops out on four sides and the enemy masses broke in great rout. The generals wished to pursue, but Zhongwei said: "Having met the enemy and kept our lives, do we still hope to win back our sons?
translations.idiomatic: A violent gale sprang up and the troops' anger boiled over. Fu Yanqing, Zhang Yanze, and others led forces out on every side and the enemy broke in rout. When the generals wanted to pursue, Zhongwei said, "We met the enemy and barely kept our lives—do you still expect to win our sons back?

sentences.zh: 」遂收軍馳歸常山。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gathered the army and galloped back to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then withdrew the army and raced back to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，重威於州內括借錢帛，吏民大被其苦，人情鹹怨，重以境內雕弊，十室九空，重威遂無留意，連上表乞歸朝，不俟報即時上路。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongwei had requisitioned money and silk within the prefecture by forced loan; officials and commoners suffered greatly from him and popular feeling was full of resentment. Moreover, within the circuit desolation prevailed and nine houses in ten stood empty. Zhongwei therefore had no further interest in staying; he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to return to court, and without waiting for a reply set out on the road at once.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had forced loans of money and cloth on the prefecture until officials and commoners alike were desperate and hatred ran deep. The circuit was ruined—nine houses in ten stood empty—and Zhongwei lost all heart for the post. He petitioned again and again to return to court and set out without waiting for a reply.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以邊上重鎮，主帥擅離，茍有奔沖，慮失禦備，然亦無如之何，即以馬全節代之，重威尋授鄴都留守。

translations.literal: The court, because this was a vital frontier post and the commander-in-chief had left his post on his own authority—if there should be a sudden enemy thrust they feared the loss of defensive preparations—yet could do nothing about it; they thereupon had Ma Quanjie replace him, and shortly Zhongwei was appointed defender of the Yedu capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew this was a vital frontier post and feared that if the commander abandoned it a sudden enemy thrust would leave them defenseless, yet it could do nothing. Ma Quanjie was sent to replace him, and Zhongwei was soon made defender of the Yedu capital.

sentences.zh: 會鎮州軍食不繼，遣殿中監王欽祚就本州和市，重威私第有粟十餘萬斛，遂錄之以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhenzhou's army provisions were not continuing; the court sent Palace Supervisor Wang Qinzuo to that prefecture to purchase grain on the market. In Zhongwei's private residence there were more than a hundred thousand hu of grain, and this was inventoried and reported.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhou ran short of rations, the court sent Palace Supervisor Wang Qinzuo to buy grain there. More than a hundred thousand hu of grain were found in Zhongwei's private storehouses and duly inventoried and reported.

sentences.zh: 朝廷給絹數萬匹，償其粟直。

translations.literal: The court gave him several tens of thousands of bolts of silk in compensation for the value of the grain.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid him with tens of thousands of bolts of silk in compensation for the grain.

sentences.zh: 重威大忿曰：「我非反逆，安得籍沒耶！

translations.literal: Zhongwei was greatly enraged and said: "I am no rebel—how can my property be confiscated!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei flew into a rage. "I am no rebel," he cried. "How can you confiscate my property?

sentences.zh: 」三年冬，晉少帝詔重威與李守貞等率師經略瀛、鄚。

translations.literal: " In the winter of the third year, the Jin Shaodi issued an edict ordering Zhongwei and Li Shouzhen and others to lead troops to conduct operations in Ying and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: " In the winter of the third year Emperor Shaodi of Jin ordered Zhongwei, Li Shouzhen, and others to lead troops against Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 師至瀛州城下，晉騎將梁漢璋與契丹接戰，漢璋死焉。

translations.literal: When the army reached below the walls of Yingzhou, the Jin cavalry general Liang Hanzhang joined battle with the Khitan and Hanzhang died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Yingzhou, the Jin cavalry general Liang Hanzhang fought the Khitan and was killed.

sentences.zh: 重威即時回軍，次武強，聞契丹主南下，乃西趨鎮州，至中渡橋，與契丹夾滹水而營。

translations.literal: Zhongwei at once turned the army back and halted at Wuqiang; hearing that the Khitan ruler was marching south, he then hurried west toward Zhenzhou, and when he reached Zhongdu Bridge he encamped facing the Khitan across the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei immediately withdrew, halting at Wuqiang. Hearing that the Khitan khan was marching south, he hurried west to Zhenzhou and encamped at Zhongdu Bridge facing the Khitan across the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 十二月八日，宋彥筠、王清等率數千人渡滹沲，陣於北岸，為敵所破。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the twelfth month, Song Yanjun, Wang Qing, and others led several thousand men across the Hutuo and formed battle lines on the north bank, but were defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth of the twelfth month Song Yanjun, Wang Qing, and others led several thousand men across the Hutuo and formed up on the north bank, only to be routed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時契丹遊軍已至欒城，道路隔絕，人情危蹙，重威密遣人詣敵帳，潛布腹心。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan raiding detachments had already reached Luancheng; roads were cut off and popular feeling was desperate. Zhongwei secretly sent men to the enemy camp to confide his inner thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raiders had already reached Luancheng, the roads were cut, and panic spread. Zhongwei secretly sent envoys to the enemy camp to sound out surrender.

sentences.zh: 契丹主大悅，許以中原帝之，重威庸暗，深以為信。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and promised to make him emperor of the Central Plains; Zhongwei was stupid and dull and deeply believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan was delighted and promised to make him emperor of the Central Plains. Dull and credulous, Zhongwei believed him completely.

sentences.zh: 一日，伏甲於內，召諸將會，告以降敵之意，諸將愕然。

translations.literal: One day he hid armed men within and summoned the generals to a meeting, telling them his intent to surrender to the enemy; the generals were stunned.
translations.idiomatic: One day he hid armed men inside, summoned the generals, and announced his plan to surrender. They were stunned.

sentences.zh: 以上將既變，乃俯首聽命，遂連署降表，令中門使高勛賫送敵帳，軍士解甲，舉聲慟哭。

translations.literal: Because the supreme commander had already changed sides, they bowed their heads and obeyed; they then jointly signed a surrender memorial, ordered Inner Gate Commissioner Gao Xun to carry it to the enemy camp, the soldiers removed their armor, and a sound of wailing rose together.
translations.idiomatic: With the supreme commander already turned traitor, they had no choice but to obey. They signed a joint surrender memorial and sent Inner Gate Commissioner Gao Xun to deliver it to the enemy camp. The soldiers laid down their arms and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 是日，有大霧起於降軍之上。

translations.literal: That day a great fog arose above the surrendering army.
translations.idiomatic: That day a heavy fog rose over the surrendering army.

sentences.zh: 契丹主使重威衣赭袍以示諸軍，尋偽加守太傅，鄴都留守如故。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler had Zhongwei wear a crimson robe to show the armies; shortly he was falsely given the additional title of Defender Grand Mentor, while his post as defender of the Yedu capital remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan had Zhongwei dress in an imperial crimson robe and parade before the armies. He was given the nominal title of Defender Grand Mentor and kept his post at Yedu.

sentences.zh: 契丹主南行，命重威部轄晉軍以從，既至東京，駐晉軍於陳橋，士伍饑凍，不勝其苦。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler marched south and ordered Zhongwei to take command of the Jin army and follow; when they reached the Eastern Capital they stationed the Jin troops at Chenqiao; officers and soldiers hungered and froze, unable to bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan marched south and made Zhongwei lead the Jin army in his train. At the Eastern Capital the Jin troops were camped at Chenqiao, where they starved and froze beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 重威每出入衢路，為市民所詬，俯首而已。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhongwei went in and out along the public roads he was reviled by the townspeople; he only bowed his head.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhongwei passed through the streets the townspeople cursed him, and he could only bow his head.

sentences.zh: 契丹下令括率京城錢帛，將相公私，雷同率配，重威與李守貞各萬緡，乃告契丹主曰：「臣等以十萬漢軍降於皇帝，不免配借，臣所不甘。

translations.literal: The Khitan issued orders to levy money and silk throughout the capital city; ministers, generals, public and private alike were assessed in uniform proportion. Zhongwei and Li Shouzhen were each assessed ten thousand strings of cash. They then told the Khitan ruler: "We have surrendered a hundred thousand Han troops to Your Majesty—yet we are not spared forced levies; this we cannot accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ordered a levy of money and silk on the capital, assessing officials and commoners alike. Zhongwei and Li Shouzhen were each assessed ten thousand strings of cash. They told the Khitan khan, "We surrendered a hundred thousand Han troops to Your Majesty, yet we are still forced to pay levies. We cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 」契丹主笑而免之。

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler laughed and exempted them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Khitan khan laughed and exempted them.

sentences.zh: 尋群盜斷澶州浮梁，契丹乃遣重威歸藩。

translations.literal: Before long bandits cut the floating bridge at Chunzhou, and the Khitan then sent Zhongwei back to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits destroyed the floating bridge at Chunzhou, and the Khitan sent Zhongwei back to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，契丹主北去，至相州城下，重威與妻石氏詣牙帳貢獻而回。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year the Khitan ruler went north; when he reached below the walls of Xiangzhou, Zhongwei and his wife Lady Shi went to the royal tent to present tribute and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year the Khitan khan marched north. When he reached Xiangzhou, Zhongwei and his wife Lady Shi went to his tent with tribute and then returned.

sentences.zh: 高祖車駕至闕，以重威為宋州節度使，加守太尉。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu's imperial carriage reached the capital he made Zhongwei military governor of Songzhou and gave him the additional title of Defender Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's imperial procession reached the capital, he made Zhongwei military governor of Songzhou and Defender Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 重威懼，閉城拒命，詔高行周率兵攻討，重威遣其子宏遂等告急於鎮州州麻答，乞師救援，旦以宏遂為質，麻答遣蕃將楊兗赴之。

translations.literal: Zhongwei was afraid, shut the city and refused to obey; an edict ordered Gao Xingzhou to lead troops to attack him. Zhongwei sent his son Hongsui and others to Zhenzhou to urge Ma Da, the prefect, to send rescue troops, offering Hongsui as hostage at dawn; Ma Da sent the tribal general Yang Yan to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhongwei shut the gates and defied the court. Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou to attack him. Zhongwei sent his son Hongsui to Ma Da at Zhenzhou begging for relief and offering Hongsui as hostage. Ma Da sent the tribal general Yang Yan to his aid.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎮州軍逐滿達勒，楊兗至洺州而回。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhenzhou army drove out Ma Da; Yang Yan reached Mingzhou and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhenzhou garrison drove out Ma Da, and Yang Yan turned back when he reached Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，高祖親征，車駕至鄴城之下，遣給事中陳觀等賫詔入城，許其歸命，重威不納。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Gaozu personally campaigned; the imperial carriage reached below Yecheng and sent Supervising Secretary Chen Guan and others bearing an edict into the city, promising that if he submitted his life would be spared; Zhongwei did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gaozu marched in person. When he reached Yecheng he sent Supervising Secretary Chen Guan and others into the city with an edict promising mercy if Zhongwei submitted. Zhongwei refused.

sentences.zh: 數日，高祖親率諸軍攻其壘，不克，王師傷夷者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Several days later the Gaozu personally led the armies to assault his ramparts but could not take them; the imperial forces had more than ten thousand killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Gaozu led the assault on the walls himself but failed to take them. More than ten thousand imperial soldiers were killed or wounded.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·杜漢徽傳》云：從高行周討杜重威於鄴城，屢為流矢所中，身被重創，猶力戰，觀者壯之。）〉

translations.literal: (The Song History, biography of Du Hanhui, says: Following Gao Xingzhou in the campaign against Du Zhongwei at Yecheng, he was repeatedly struck by stray arrows, his body bore grave wounds, yet he still fought fiercely; those who watched were impressed by his valor.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History biography of Du Hanhui records that in Gao Xingzhou's campaign against Du Zhongwei at Yecheng he was hit again and again by stray arrows and bore grave wounds, yet still fought on fiercely to the admiration of all who watched.)

sentences.zh: 高祖駐軍數旬，城中糧盡，屑麹餅以給軍士，吏民逾壘而出者甚眾，皆無人色。

translations.literal: The Gaozu encamped his army for several tens of days; within the city grain was exhausted and they ground chaff into cakes to supply the soldiers. Very many officials and commoners climbed over the ramparts to get out, all without human color in their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu besieged the city for weeks until grain ran out and the defenders ground chaff into cakes to feed the troops. Crowds of officials and commoners climbed over the walls to escape, their faces gray as death.

sentences.zh: 至是，重威牙將詣行宮請降，復遣節度判官王敏奉表請罪，賜優詔敦勉，許其如初。

translations.literal: At this point one of Zhongwei's military adjutants went to the mobile palace to request surrender; he again sent his circuit administrative aide Wang Min bearing a memorial begging forgiveness. A gracious edict was bestowed encouraging him, and he was permitted to return to his former status.
translations.idiomatic: At last one of Zhongwei's adjutants came to the imperial camp to surrender. Wang Min was sent with a memorial begging pardon. Gaozu issued a gracious edict of encouragement and promised to treat him as before.

sentences.zh: 重威即遣其子宏遂、妻石氏出候高祖，重威繼踵出降，素服俟罪，復其衣冠，賜見，即日制授檢校太師、守太傅、兼中書令。

translations.literal: Zhongwei at once sent out his son Hongsui and his wife Lady Shi to wait upon the Gaozu; Zhongwei followed in their steps to surrender, wearing plain clothes to await punishment, then restored his robes and cap, was granted an audience, and that same day by imperial order was made Honorary Grand Preceptor, Defender Grand Tutor, and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei sent out his son Hongsui and his wife Lady Shi to wait on Gaozu, then followed to surrender in plain dress to await judgment. Restored to his robes, he was received in audience and that same day appointed Honorary Grand Preceptor, Defender Grand Tutor, and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鄴城士庶，殍殕者十之六七。

translations.literal: Among the gentry and commoners of Yecheng, six or seven in ten died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven people in ten among the population of Yecheng had starved to death.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹遣幽州指揮使張璉，以部下軍二千餘人屯鄴，時亦有燕軍一千五百人在京師，會高祖至闕，有上變者，言燕軍謀亂，盡誅於繁臺之下，咸稱其冤。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan had sent Zhang Lian, commander of Youzhou, to garrison Yecheng with more than two thousand troops under his command. At that time there were also fifteen hundred Yan troops in the capital. When the Gaozu reached the capital, someone reported a plot of rebellion by the Yan troops and they were all executed below Fantai; all called it a wrongful killing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan had sent Youzhou commander Zhang Lian to garrison Yecheng with more than two thousand men. Fifteen hundred Yan troops were also in the capital. When Gaozu reached the throne, someone reported that the Yan troops were plotting rebellion and they were all executed below Fantai—a killing widely called unjust.

sentences.zh: 有逃奔於鄴者，備言其事，故張璉等懼死，與重威膠固守城，略無叛誌。

translations.literal: Some who had fled to Yecheng told the whole affair in detail; therefore Zhang Lian and the others feared death, clung to Zhongwei in holding the city fast, and had not the slightest thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives who reached Yecheng told the whole story, so Zhang Lian and his men, fearing death, clung to Zhongwei and held the city with no thought of surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦悔其前失，累令宣諭，許以不死。

translations.literal: The Gaozu also regretted his earlier mistake and repeatedly ordered proclamations assuring them they would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu too regretted his earlier mistake and repeatedly proclaimed that they would not be executed.

sentences.zh: 璉等於城上揚言曰：「繁臺之誅，燕軍何罪？

translations.literal: Zhang Lian and the others shouted from atop the wall: "At the execution at Fantai, what crime had the Yan troops committed?
translations.idiomatic: From the walls Zhang Lian and his men cried out, "What crime had the Yan troops committed at Fantai?

sentences.zh: 既無生理，以死為期。

translations.literal: Since we have no chance of life, we take death as our term.
translations.idiomatic: We have no hope of life—only death awaits us.

sentences.zh: 」璉一軍在圍中，重威推食解衣，盡力姑息。

translations.literal: " Zhang Lian's whole army was within the siege; Zhongwei shared his food and gave them his clothing, doing his utmost to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Lian's entire force was trapped in the siege, and Zhongwei shared his food and clothing and did everything he could to placate them.

sentences.zh: 燕軍驕悍，憑陵吏民，子女金帛，公行豪奪。

translations.literal: The Yan troops were arrogant and fierce; they bullied officials and commoners, and with women, children, gold, and silk they openly committed violent seizure.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops were arrogant and brutal. They bullied officials and commoners and openly seized their women, children, gold, and silk.

sentences.zh: 及重威請命，璉等邀朝廷信誓，詔許璉等卻歸本土。

translations.literal: When Zhongwei begged for his life, Zhang Lian and the others demanded a sworn pledge from the court; an edict promised that Zhang Lian and the others might return to their native territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwei sued for mercy, Zhang Lian and his men demanded a sworn pledge from the court. An edict promised they could return home.

sentences.zh: 及出降，盡誅璉等將數十人，其什長已下放歸幽州，將出漢境，剽略而去。

translations.literal: When they came out to surrender, several tens of Zhang Lian's officers were all executed. Their squad leaders and below had already been sent back to Youzhou; as they were about to leave Han territory they plundered on their way out.
translations.idiomatic: After the surrender dozens of Zhang Lian's officers were executed. The squad leaders and rank and file had already been sent back toward Youzhou, but as they left Han territory they looted their way out.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣三司使王章、樞密副使郭威，錄重威部下將吏盡誅之，籍其財產與重威私帑，分給將士。

translations.literal: The Gaozu sent Commissioner of the Three Departments Wang Zhang and Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Guo Wei to register Zhongwei's subordinate officers and officials and execute them all; their property and Zhongwei's private treasury were inventoried and distributed among the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Commissioner of the Three Departments Wang Zhang and Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Guo Wei to register all of Zhongwei's officers and officials and execute them. Their property and Zhongwei's private treasury were inventoried and distributed among the troops.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，高祖不豫，既而大漸。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned to the palace; the Gaozu was unwell, and shortly entered his final decline.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Gaozu fell ill and soon sank into his final decline.

sentences.zh: 顧命之際，謂近臣將佐曰：「善防重威。

translations.literal: At the moment of his final charge he said to his close ministers and military aides: "Take good care to guard against Zhongwei.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his closest ministers and generals, "Guard yourselves well against Zhongwei.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，遂收重威，重威子宏璋、宏璉、宏傑誅之。

translations.literal: " When the emperor died, Zhongwei was at once arrested; Zhongwei's sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongjie were executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor died, Zhongwei was seized and executed together with his sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongjie.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「杜重威猶貯禍心，未悛逆節，梟音不改，虺性難馴。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Du Zhongwei still harbors a treacherous heart and has not repented of his rebellious conduct; the owl's cry he does not change, the viper's nature is hard to tame.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Du Zhongwei still nurses treachery in his heart and has not repented of his rebellion. The owl's cry is unchanged; the viper's nature cannot be tamed.

sentences.zh: 昨朕小有不安，罷朝數日，而重威父子潛肆兇言，怨謗大朝，扇惑小輩；

translations.literal: Yesterday when We were slightly unwell and suspended court for several days, Zhongwei father and son secretly uttered murderous words, slandered the great court, and incited petty men;
translations.idiomatic: When I was briefly unwell and suspended court for several days, Zhongwei and his sons secretly spread seditious talk, slandered the throne, and incited the rabble;

sentences.zh: 今則顯有陳告，備驗奸期。

translations.literal: now there are open denunciations and the full verification of their treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: now denunciations have come forward and their treacherous plot is fully confirmed.

sentences.zh: 既負深恩，須置極法，其杜重威父子並處斬。

translations.literal: Having betrayed deep grace, they must be subjected to the extreme penalty: Du Zhongwei father and son are all to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Having betrayed deep favor, they must suffer the utmost penalty. Du Zhongwei and his sons are all to be executed.

sentences.zh: 所有晉朝公主及外親族，一切如常，仍與供給。

translations.literal: As for all princesses of the Jin dynasty and collateral kin by marriage, everything is to be as before, and provision is still to be made for them.
translations.idiomatic: All princesses of the Jin dynasty and their affinal kin are to be treated as before and continue to receive support.

sentences.zh: 」重威父子已誅，陳屍於通衢，都人聚觀者詬罵蹴擊，軍吏不能禁，屍首狼籍，斯須而盡。

translations.literal: " After Zhongwei father and son had been executed, their corpses were displayed in the public thoroughfare. The people of the capital who gathered to watch reviled them, kicked and struck them; military officers could not restrain them, and the corpses were torn to pieces in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: " After the executions their bodies were displayed in the street. Crowds of the capital cursed them and kicked and struck the corpses until the guards could not hold them back. In moments the bodies were torn to shreds.

sentences.zh: 宏璉，重威之子也，累官至陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Honglian was a son of Zhongwei; he rose through repeated offices to prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Honglian, a son of Zhongwei, rose through the ranks to prefect of Chenzhou.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》：黨進，幼為天雄軍節度使杜重威奴，重威愛其淳謹，雖長，猶令與婢妾雜侍。

translations.literal: (The Longping ji says: Dang Jin in his youth was a slave of Du Zhongwei, military governor of the Tianxiong army; Zhongwei loved his simple honesty, and though he grew up still had him wait together with maidservants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: (The Longping ji records that Dang Jin was in his youth a slave of Du Zhongwei, military governor of Tianxiong. Zhongwei prized his simple honesty and, even after he grew up, still had him wait among the maidservants and concubines.

sentences.zh: 重威敗，周祖得之，以為鐵騎都虞候。

translations.literal: When Zhongwei was defeated, the Zhou founder obtained him and made him chief controller of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwei fell, the founder of Zhou took him into service and made him chief controller of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 重威之後寒餓，進常分俸以給，士大夫或愧焉。）〉

translations.literal: After Zhongwei's downfall he suffered cold and hunger; Jin regularly divided his salary to supply him, and some scholar-officials felt ashamed by this.)
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongwei's ruin he fell into want. Jin regularly shared his salary to support him, to the shame of some scholar-officials.)

sentences.zh: 李守貞，河陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen was a man of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen was a native of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 少桀黠落魄，事本部為牙將。

translations.literal: In his youth he was fierce, cunning, and down on his luck; he served his home command as a military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever, unruly, and down on his luck, and served his home command as a military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖鎮河陽，用為典客，後移數鎮，皆從之。

translations.literal: When the Jin Gaozu governed Heyang he employed him as master of guests; afterward when he shifted through several garrisons, Shouzhen followed him in each.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin governed Heyang he employed him as master of guests. When Gaozu moved through several postings, Shouzhen followed him each time.

sentences.zh: 及即位，累遷至客省使。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Shouzhen was repeatedly promoted until he reached the post of commissioner of the guest bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shouzhen rose step by step to commissioner of the guest bureau.

sentences.zh: 天福中，李金全以安州叛，淮夷入寇，晉高祖命馬全節討之，守貞監護其軍，賊平，守貞為宣徽使。

translations.literal: During Tianfu, Li Jinquan rebelled with Anzhou; the Huai barbarians invaded; the Jin Gaozu ordered Ma Quanjie to campaign against them, with Shouzhen supervising the army. When the bandits were pacified, Shouzhen became commissioner of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, Li Jinquan rebelled at Anzhou and Huai tribes invaded. Gaozu sent Ma Quanjie to suppress them with Shouzhen supervising the army. After the rebels were crushed, Shouzhen became commissioner of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，授滑州節度兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使，未幾，改侍衛都虞候。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded to the throne, Shouzhen was given the posts of military governor of Huazhou and commander of the palace guard cavalry; before long he was changed to chief controller of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shaodi came to the throne, Shouzhen was made military governor of Huazhou and commander of the palace guard cavalry, then soon made chief controller of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 開運元年春，敵眾犯澶、魏，少帝幸澶州，契丹遣將麻答以奇兵由鄆州馬家口濟河，立柵於東岸，守貞率師自澶州馳赴之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun the enemy masses invaded Chun and Wei; Emperor Shaodi visited Chunzhou. The Khitan sent the general Ma Da with a surprise force to cross the river at Majiakou in Yanzhou and erect palisades on the east bank. Shouzhen led troops in haste from Chunzhou to go to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first Kaiyun year the enemy invaded Chun and Wei, and Emperor Shaodi went to Chunzhou. The Khitan sent Ma Da with a surprise force across the river at Majiakou in Yanzhou and threw up palisades on the east bank. Shouzhen raced from Chunzhou to meet them.

sentences.zh: 契丹大敗，溺死者數千人，獲馬數百匹，偏裨七十餘人。

translations.literal: The Khitan suffered a great defeat; several thousand drowned; several hundred horses were captured, and more than seventy junior officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were routed. Several thousand drowned, several hundred horses were captured, and more than seventy officers were taken.

sentences.zh: 有頃，敵退。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝還京，以守貞為兗州節度使，依前侍衛都虞候。

translations.literal: The Jin Shaodi returned to the capital and made Shouzhen military governor of Yanzhou, while he retained his former post as chief controller of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shaodi of Jin returned to the capital and made Shouzhen military governor of Yanzhou while keeping him as chief controller of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 五月，以守貞為青州行營都部署，率兵二萬東討楊光遠，命符彥卿為副。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Shouzhen was made overall commander of the Qingzhou field camp and led twenty thousand troops east to campaign against Yang Guangyuan; Fu Yanqing was ordered as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Shouzhen was made overall commander of the Qingzhou field army and led twenty thousand men east against Yang Guangyuan, with Fu Yanqing as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 十一月，光遠子承勛等乞降，守貞入城，害光遠於別第。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Yang Guangyuan's son Chengxun and others begged to surrender; Shouzhen entered the city and killed Guangyuan in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yang Guangyuan's son Chengxun and others sued for surrender. Shouzhen entered the city and killed Guangyuan in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 光遠有孔目官吏宋顏者，盡以光遠財寶、名姬、善馬告於守貞，得之置於帳下。

translations.literal: Guangyuan had a clerical officer named Song Yan who disclosed all of Guangyuan's treasure, famous beauties, and fine horses to Shouzhen; obtaining them, Shouzhen placed them in his own camp.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan had a clerk named Song Yan who revealed all of his treasure, famous beauties, and fine horses to Shouzhen. Shouzhen took them for his own camp.

sentences.zh: 近例，官軍克復城隍，必降德音，洗滌瑕穢，時樞密使桑維翰以光遠同惡數十輩潛竄未出，搜索甚急，故制書久不下。

translations.literal: By recent precedent, when the imperial army recovered a walled city a gracious edict was always issued to wash away stains and faults. At that time the Director of the Palace Secretariat Sang Weihan, because several tens of Guangyuan's fellow evildoers were still in hiding and had not come forth and the search was very urgent, therefore the imperial order was long in not being issued.
translations.idiomatic: By recent custom, when the imperial army recovered a city a gracious edict was issued to absolve the people. But Director of the Palace Secretariat Sang Weihan, because dozens of Guangyuan's accomplices were still in hiding and the hunt was intense, delayed the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 或有告宋顏匿於守貞處者，朝廷取而殺之，守貞由是怨維翰。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Song Yan was hidden at Shouzhen's place; the court took him and executed him, and from this Shouzhen bore resentment toward Weihan.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Song Yan was hidden with Shouzhen, the court seized and executed him. Shouzhen henceforth resented Weihan.

sentences.zh: 時行營將士所給賞賜，守貞盡以黦茶、染木、姜藥之類分給之，軍中大怨，乃以帛包所得物，如人首級，目之為守貞頭，懸於樹以詛之。

translations.literal: At that time the rewards given to the field-camp officers and soldiers—Shouzhen distributed them entirely in the form of dark tea, dyewood, ginger, medicines, and the like. Great resentment arose in the army; they wrapped what they had received in cloth like human heads, called them "Shouzhen's heads," and hung them on trees to curse him.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards given to the field army Shouzhen distributed entirely as dark tea, dyewood, ginger, and medicines. The troops were furious. They wrapped the goods in cloth like severed heads, called them "Shouzhen's heads," and hung them on trees to curse him.

sentences.zh: 守貞班師，加同平章事，以楊光遠東京第賜之。

translations.literal: Shouzhen returned the army in triumph and was given the additional title of Grand Councilor; Yang Guangyuan's residence in the Eastern Capital was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzhen returned in triumph he was made Grand Councilor and given Yang Guangyuan's mansion in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 守貞因取連宅軍營，以廣其第，大興土木，治之歲餘，為京師之甲。

translations.literal: Shouzhen thereupon took adjoining military camps to enlarge his residence, undertook great construction in earth and timber, and worked on it for more than a year until it was the finest in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He seized adjoining army camps to enlarge his estate and spent more than a year on lavish construction until it was the finest mansion in the capital.

sentences.zh: 行幸賜宴，恩禮無比。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses he was granted banquets; favor and ceremony were without parallel.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progresses he was honored with banquets whose favor and ceremony had no equal.

sentences.zh: 開運二年春，契丹以全軍南下，前鋒至相州湯陰縣，詔守貞屯滑州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaiyun, the Khitan marched south with their entire army; the vanguard reached Tangyin County in Xiangzhou, and an edict ordered Shouzhen to encamp at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Kaiyun 2 the Khitan marched south with their full army. When the vanguard reached Tangyin in Xiangzhou, an edict ordered Li Shouzhen to encamp at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 少帝再幸澶州，以守貞為北面行營都監，與招討使杜重威北伐，洎獲陽城之捷，遂收軍而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Shaodi again visited Chanzhou. Shouzhen was made overall inspector of the northern field camp and, together with punitive commissioner Du Zhongwei, marched north. After winning the victory at Yangcheng, they withdrew the army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shaodi again went to Chanzhou. Li Shouzhen was made overall inspector of the northern field camp and marched north with punitive commissioner Du Zhongwei. After the victory at Yangcheng they withdrew and returned.

sentences.zh: 四月，車駕還京，以守貞為侍衛副都指揮使，移鎮宋州，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the imperial carriage returned to the capital. Shouzhen was made deputy overall commander of the palace guard, transferred to govern Songzhou, and given the additional title of Honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor returned to the capital. Shouzhen was made deputy overall commander of the palace guard, transferred to Songzhou, and given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 三年春，詔守貞率師巡邊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, an edict ordered Shouzhen to lead troops on a border patrol.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year an edict ordered Shouzhen to lead troops on a border patrol.

sentences.zh: 至衡水，獲鄚州刺史趙思英而還。

translations.literal: When he reached Hengshui, he captured Mozhou prefect Zhao Siying and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengshui he captured Mozhou prefect Zhao Siying and returned.

sentences.zh: 居無何，代高行周為侍衛親軍都指揮使，移鎮鄆州，意頗觖望。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as overall commander of the palace guard corps, transferred to govern Yanzhou, and was rather dissatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as overall commander of the palace guard and was transferred to Yanzhou, where he nursed considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 會宰臣李崧加侍中，守貞謂樞密使直學士殷鵬曰：「樞密何功，便加正相！

translations.literal: It happened that chief councilor Li Song was given the additional title of Palace Attendant. Shouzhen said to Yin Peng, academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs: "What merit has the Bureau of Military Affairs that he should be made a chief councilor!
translations.idiomatic: When chief councilor Li Song was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, Shouzhen said to Yin Peng, academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, "What has the Bureau of Military Affairs done to deserve a chief councilorship!

sentences.zh: 」先是，桑維翰以元勛舊德為樞密使，守貞位望素處其下，每憚之，與李彥韜、馮玉輩協力排斥，維翰竟罷樞務。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Sang Weihan had served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs by virtue of his founding merit and old standing. Shouzhen's rank and prestige had always been below his, and he feared him on every occasion. Together with Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and their set he worked to drive him out, until Weihan was at last removed from bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Sang Weihan had held the Bureau of Military Affairs by virtue of founding merit and long service. Shouzhen had always ranked below him and feared him. Together with Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and their faction he worked to drive Sang out until Weihan was finally removed from bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 李崧事分疏遠，守貞得以淩蔑。

translations.literal: Li Song's duties kept him at a distance; Shouzhen was therefore able to treat him with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song's duties kept him at a distance, and Shouzhen was free to treat him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，契丹寇邊，以守貞為北面行營都部署。

translations.literal: That summer the Khitan raided the border, and Shouzhen was made overall commander of the northern field camp.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the Khitan raided the frontier, Shouzhen was made overall commander of the northern field camp.

sentences.zh: 少帝開曲宴於內殿，以寵其行，教坊令人獻語云：「天子不須憂北寇，守貞面上管幽州。

translations.literal: Emperor Shaodi held an informal banquet in an inner hall to honor his departure. Entertainers from the Music Bureau presented a rhyme saying: "The Son of Heaven need not worry about northern invaders—Shouzhen's face will take care of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shaodi held an intimate banquet in an inner hall to honor his departure. Entertainers from the Music Bureau offered a rhyme: "The Son of Heaven need not worry about northern invaders—Shouzhen's face will take care of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 」既罷，守貞有自負之色，以其言誇詫於外。

translations.literal: " When the banquet ended, Shouzhen wore a self-satisfied look and boasted of the words outside.
translations.idiomatic: " When the banquet ended Shouzhen wore a self-satisfied look and boasted of the words abroad.

sentences.zh: 既而率兵至定州北，與契丹偏師遇，斬蕃將嘉哩而還。

translations.literal: Presently he led troops north of Dingzhou, met a Khitan detachment, beheaded the barbarian general Jiali, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops north of Dingzhou, met a Khitan detachment, beheaded the Khitan general Jiali, and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was further given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣瀛州刺史偽降於少帝，請發大軍應接，朝廷信之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan sent the prefect of Yingzhou to feign surrender to Emperor Shaodi and request that a great army be sent to meet him; the court believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then sent the prefect of Yingzhou to feign surrender to Emperor Shaodi and ask for a great army to meet him, and the court believed the ruse.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔杜重威為北面行營招討使，以守貞為兵馬都監，知幽州行府事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict appointed Du Zhongwei punitive commissioner of the northern field camp, with Shouzhen as overall inspector of horse and foot and administrator of the mobile headquarters at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict made Du Zhongwei punitive commissioner of the northern field camp and Shouzhen overall inspector of horse and foot with charge of the mobile headquarters at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，守貞領兵再由鄴都，杜重威厚加贈遺，曲意承迎，守貞悅之，每於帝前稱舉，請委征討之柄。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouzhen had led troops through Yedu again, Du Zhongwei had lavished gifts upon him and flattered him to the utmost. Shouzhen was pleased, and repeatedly praised him before the emperor, asking that the command of the campaign be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shouzhen had led troops through Yedu again, Du Zhongwei had showered him with gifts and flattered him to the utmost. Shouzhen was pleased and repeatedly praised him before the emperor, asking that command of the campaign be entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 至是，守貞、重威等會兵於鄴，遂趨瀛州，瀛州不應。

translations.literal: At this point Shouzhen, Zhongwei, and the others mustered troops at Ye, then hurried toward Yingzhou, but Yingzhou gave no response.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Shouzhen, Zhongwei, and the others gathered at Ye and marched on Yingzhou, but Yingzhou made no response.

sentences.zh: 貝州節度使梁漢璋為蕃將高牟翰所敗，死之，王師遂還。

translations.literal: Beizhou military governor Liang Hanzhang was defeated by the barbarian general Gao Mouhan and killed; the imperial army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Beizhou military governor Liang Hanzhang was defeated and killed by the Khitan general Gao Mouhan, and the imperial army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 師至深州，聞契丹大至，乃西趨鎮州，至滹沲之中渡，與敵相遇，官軍營於滹水之南。

translations.literal: When the army reached Shenzhou and heard that the Khitan had arrived in force, it hurried west toward Zhenzhou. At Zhongdu ford on the Hutuo River it met the enemy. The imperial army encamped south of the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Shenzhou and heard that the Khitan were coming in force, it hurried west to Zhenzhou. At Zhongdu ford on the Hutuo it met the enemy and encamped south of the river.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敵騎潛渡至欒城，斷我糧路，尋則王清戰死，杜重威遂與守貞歸命契丹，授守貞司徒，依前鄆州節度使，從契丹至汴。

translations.literal: Before long enemy cavalry secretly crossed the river and reached Luancheng, cutting the grain route. Presently Wang Qing died in battle. Du Zhongwei then surrendered to the Khitan together with Shouzhen. Shouzhen was appointed Minister of Education and remained military governor of Yanzhou as before. He followed the Khitan to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Khitan cavalry secretly crossed the river to Luancheng and cut the supply line. Wang Qing soon fell in battle. Du Zhongwei then surrendered to the Khitan together with Shouzhen. Shouzhen was made Minister of Education and kept his post as military governor of Yanzhou, then followed the Khitan to Bian.

sentences.zh: 時京輦之下，契丹充斥，都人士庶，若在塗炭。

translations.literal: At that time beneath the imperial capital the Khitan filled the land; gentry and commoners in the capital were as if in fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan filled the capital, and gentry and commoners alike suffered as if in fire and water.

sentences.zh: 二帥出入揚揚，市人詬之，略無慚色。

translations.literal: The two commanders went in and out with swagger; market people reviled them, yet they showed not the least shame.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders swaggered in and out of the city while market folk cursed them, yet they showed not the least shame.

sentences.zh: 有頃，河北及京東草寇大起，澶州浮橋為群賊所斷，契丹主甚恐，乃命諸帥各歸本鎮，守貞遂赴汶陽。

translations.literal: After a time grass-bandits rose in great numbers in Hebei and east of the capital. The floating bridge at Chanzhou was cut by the bandit bands. The Khitan ruler was greatly afraid and thereupon ordered each commander to return to his original garrison. Shouzhen then set out for Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long grass-bandits rose in great numbers in Hebei and east of the capital, and the floating bridge at Chanzhou was cut by rebel bands. The Khitan khan was greatly alarmed and ordered each commander back to his original post. Shouzhen then went to Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖入汴，守貞懼而來朝，授守貞太保，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Bian, Shouzhen came to court in fear. He was appointed Defender Grand Mentor and transferred to govern Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Bian, Shouzhen came to court in fear. He was made Defender Grand Mentor and transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 居無何，高祖晏駕，杜重威被誅，守貞愈不自安，乃潛畜異計。

translations.literal: Before long Gaozu died. Du Zhongwei was executed. Shouzhen grew ever more ill at ease and secretly nursed disloyal designs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gaozu died and Du Zhongwei was executed. Shouzhen grew ever more uneasy and secretly nursed treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年三月，先致書於權臣，布求保證，而完城郭，繕甲兵，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Qianyou he first sent letters to powerful ministers seeking guarantees, while completing the walls and moats, repairing armor and weapons, day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Qianyou 1 he first wrote to powerful ministers seeking guarantees, while completing walls and moats and repairing armor and weapons day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 守貞以漢室新造，嗣君才立，自謂舉無遺策，又有僧總倫者，以占術幹守貞，謂守貞有人君之位，

translations.literal: Shouzhen thought that since the Han house was newly established and the succeeding ruler had only just taken the throne, every move he made would succeed without omission. There was also a monk named Zonglun who pressed his claim upon Shouzhen with divination, saying that Shouzhen had the position of a ruler,
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen thought the Han house newly founded and the heir only just enthroned, and believed every move he made would succeed. There was also a monk named Zonglun who pressed him with divination, saying that Shouzhen had the destiny of a ruler,

translations.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian says: Junyi native Zhao Xiuji had long been skilled in numerology. Since Shouzhen governed Huazhou he was appointed administrative aide for household registration and followed him through each transfer of garrison.
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian says: Zhao Xiuji of Junyi had long been skilled in numerology. Since Shouzhen governed Huazhou he had been appointed administrative aide for household registration and had followed him through each transfer of post.

sentences.zh: 為守貞言：「時命不可妄動。

translations.literal: He told Shouzhen: "The times are not right for rash action.
translations.idiomatic: He told Shouzhen, "The times are not right for rash action.

sentences.zh: 」前後切諫非一，守貞不聽，乃稱疾歸裏。）〉

translations.idiomatic: " He remonstrated urgently again and again, but Shouzhen would not listen, so he claimed illness and returned home.)〉

sentences.zh: 未幾，趙思綰以京兆叛，遣使奉表送禦衣於守貞，守貞自謂天時人事合符於己，乃潛結草賊，令所在竊發，遣兵據潼關。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Siwan rebelled at Jingzhao and sent envoys bearing a memorial and presenting imperial robes to Shouzhen. Shouzhen took it that heaven, the times, and human affairs all matched him, and secretly allied with grass-bandits, ordering uprisings wherever they could be incited, and sent troops to seize Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao Siwan rebelled at Jingzhao and sent envoys with a memorial and imperial robes to Shouzhen. Shouzhen took it that heaven, the times, and human affairs all favored him. He secretly allied with bandits, incited uprisings wherever he could, and sent troops to seize Tong Pass.

translations.literal: (The Song History, Biography of Wang Jili: In Li Shouzhen's rebellion he ordered Jili to hold Tong Pass, but Jili was defeated by Guo Congyi.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History, Biography of Wang Jili, records that in Li Shouzhen's rebellion he ordered Jili to hold Tong Pass, but Jili was defeated by Guo Congyi.)〉

sentences.zh: 朝廷命白文珂、常思等領兵問罪，復遣樞密使郭威西征。

translations.literal: The court ordered Bai Wenke, Chang Si, and others to lead troops to punish him, and again sent Bureau commissioner Guo Wei on a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Bai Wenke, Chang Si, and others to lead troops against him and again sent Bureau commissioner Guo Wei on a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 官軍初至，守貞以諸軍多曾隸於麾下，自謂素得軍情，坐俟扣城迎己，及軍士詬噪，大失所望。

translations.literal: When the imperial army first arrived, Shouzhen thought that many of the troops had once served under him and that he had long won their hearts; he sat waiting for them to knock at the walls to welcome him. When the soldiers shouted abuse instead, he was deeply disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army first arrived, Shouzhen thought many of the troops had once served under him and that he had long held their loyalty. He sat waiting for them to knock at the walls and welcome him. When the soldiers shouted abuse instead, he was deeply disappointed.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·馬全義傳》：李守貞鎮河中，召置帳下。

translations.literal: (The Song History, Biography of Ma Quanyi: When Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong he summoned Quanyi to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History, Biography of Ma Quanyi, records that when Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong he summoned Quanyi to his staff.

sentences.zh: 及守貞叛，周主討之，全義每率敢死士夜出攻周祖壘，多所殺傷。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen rebelled, the Later Zhou ruler campaigned against him. Quanyi often led dare-death troops out at night to attack the Zhou founder's camp and killed or wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzhen rebelled, the Zhou ruler campaigned against him. Quanyi often led dare-death troops out at night to attack the Zhou founder's camp and killed or wounded many.

sentences.zh: 守貞貪而無謀，性多忌刻，全義累為畫策，皆不能用。）〉

translations.literal: Shouzhen was greedy and without strategy, and by nature jealous and harsh. Quanyi repeatedly plotted for him, but none of it could be used.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was greedy and unstrategic, and by nature jealous and harsh. Quanyi repeatedly offered plans, but none could be used.)〉

sentences.zh: 俄而王景崇據岐下，與趙思綰遣使推奉，守貞乃自號秦王，思綰、景崇皆受守貞署置。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Jingchong held the Qi region and, together with Zhao Siwan, sent envoys to proclaim Shouzhen's elevation. Shouzhen thereupon styled himself King of Qin; Siwan and Jingchong both accepted appointments from him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Jingchong held the Qi region and, together with Zhao Siwan, sent envoys to proclaim Shouzhen's elevation. Shouzhen styled himself King of Qin, and Siwan and Jingchong both accepted appointments from him.

sentences.zh: 又遣人賫蠟彈於吳、蜀、契丹，以求應援。

translations.literal: He also sent men bearing wax-sealed dispatches to Wu, Shu, and the Khitan to seek reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys bearing wax-sealed dispatches to Wu, Shu, and the Khitan to seek reinforcements.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書·朱元傳》：守貞以河中反，漢命周太祖討之，元與李平奉守貞表來乞師，未復而守貞敗。）〉

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang, Biography of Zhu Yuan: When Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, the Han ordered Zhou Taizu to suppress him. Yuan and Li Ping came bearing Shouzhen's memorial to beg troops, but before they returned Shouzhen had already been defeated.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang, Biography of Zhu Yuan, records that when Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong the Han ordered Zhou Taizu to suppress him. Zhu Yuan and Li Ping came bearing Shouzhen's memorial to beg troops, but before they returned Shouzhen had already been defeated.)〉

sentences.zh: 既而城中糧盡，殺人為食。

translations.literal: Presently grain in the city ran out and they killed people for food.
translations.idiomatic: Before long grain in the city ran out and the defenders killed people for food.

sentences.zh: 召總倫詰其休咎，總倫至曰：「王自有天分，人不能奪。

translations.literal: Shouzhen summoned Zonglun to question him about fortune and disaster. Zonglun arrived and said: "Your Majesty has the mandate of heaven; no man can take it away.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen summoned Zonglun to ask about fortune and disaster. When Zonglun arrived he said, "Your Majesty has heaven's mandate; no man can take it away.

sentences.zh: 然分野災變，俟磨滅將盡，存留一人一騎，即王鵲起之際也。

translations.literal: Yet there are calamities in your allotted region. Wait until they are worn nearly away and only one man and one horse remain—that will be the moment for Your Majesty to rise like the magpie.
translations.idiomatic: Yet calamities afflict your allotted region. Wait until they are nearly worn away and only one man and one horse remain—that will be the moment for Your Majesty to rise like the magpie.

sentences.zh: 」守貞深以為信。

translations.literal: " Shouzhen deeply believed it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouzhen believed it completely.

sentences.zh: 洎攻城，守貞欲發石以拒外軍，炮竿子不可得，無何，上遊泛一筏至，其木悉可為炮竿，守貞以為神助。

translations.literal: When the siege pressed on, Shouzhen wished to deploy catapults to repel the outside army but could not obtain throwing-pole timber. Before long a raft floated down from upstream; its timber could all serve as throwing poles. Shouzhen took it for divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege pressed on, Shouzhen wished to deploy catapults against the besiegers but could not obtain throwing-pole timber. Before long a raft floated down from upstream; all its timber could serve as throwing poles. Shouzhen took it for divine aid.

sentences.zh: 又嘗因宴會將佐，守貞執弧矢，遙指一虎舐掌圖曰：「我若有非常之事，當中虎舌。

translations.literal: On another occasion, while feasting his officers, Shouzhen took bow and arrow and, from afar, pointed at a painting of a tiger licking its paw and said: "If I undertake something extraordinary, I shall hit the tiger's tongue.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while feasting his officers, Shouzhen took bow and arrow and, from afar, pointed at a painting of a tiger licking its paw and said, "If I undertake something extraordinary, I shall hit the tiger's tongue.

sentences.zh: 」引弓一發中之，左右拜賀，守貞亦自負焉。

translations.literal: " He drew the bow and loosed once; the arrow struck true. Those left and right bowed in congratulation, and Shouzhen was self-satisfied as well.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew the bow and loosed once; the arrow struck true. Those around him bowed in congratulation, and Shouzhen was self-satisfied as well.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·吳虔裕傳》：周祖討三叛，以虔裕為河中行營都監，率護聖諸軍五千以往。

translations.literal: (The Song History, Biography of Wu Qianyu: The Zhou founder suppressed the Three Rebellions and made Qianyu overall inspector of the Hezhong field camp, leading five thousand troops of the Imperial Guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History, Biography of Wu Qianyu, records that when the Zhou founder suppressed the Three Rebellions he made Qianyu overall inspector of the Hezhong field camp and led five thousand Imperial Guard troops there.

sentences.zh: 李守貞出兵五千餘，設梯橋，分五路於長連城西北以禦周祖。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen sent out more than five thousand men, set up ladder-bridges, and divided into five routes northwest of Changliancheng to resist the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen sent out more than five thousand men, set up ladder-bridges, and divided into five routes northwest of Changliancheng to resist the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 周祖令虔裕率大軍橫擊之，蒲人敗走，奪其梯橋，殺傷大半。）〉

translations.literal: The Zhou founder ordered Qianyu to lead the main army in a lateral strike. The men of Pu were defeated and fled; their ladder-bridges were seized and more than half were killed or wounded.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder ordered Qianyu to lead the main army in a lateral strike. The men of Pu were routed, their ladder-bridges were seized, and more than half were killed or wounded.)〉

sentences.zh: 及周光遜以西寨降，其勢益窘，人情離散。

translations.literal: When Zhou Guangxun surrendered the western fort, their position grew ever tighter and popular feeling scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Guangxun surrendered the western fort, their position grew ever tighter and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻城愈急，守貞乃潛於衙署多積薪芻，為自焚之計。

translations.literal: The imperial army pressed the siege ever harder. Shouzhen secretly piled much firewood and fodder in the yamen compound, planning to burn himself.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army pressed the siege ever harder. Shouzhen secretly piled firewood and fodder in the yamen compound, planning to burn himself.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，城陷，舉家蹈火而死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year the city fell. The whole household walked into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year the city fell. The whole household walked into the fire and perished.

sentences.zh: 王師入城，於煙中獲其屍，斷其首函之，並獲數子二女，與其黨俱獻於闕下。

translations.literal: When the imperial army entered the city they recovered his corpse from the smoke, severed his head and boxed it, and also captured several sons and two daughters together with his faction; all were presented at the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army entered the city they recovered his corpse from the smoke, severed his head and boxed it, and also captured several sons and two daughters together with his faction. All were presented at court.

sentences.zh: 隱帝御明德樓受俘馘，宣露布，百僚稱賀。

translations.literal: Emperor Yin mounted the Hall of Mingde to receive the captives and severed heads, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yin mounted the Hall of Mingde to receive the captives and severed heads, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，以俘馘徇於都城，守貞首級梟於南市，諸子並賊黨孫願、劉芮、張延嗣、劉仁裕、僧總倫、靖余、張球、王廷秀、焦文傑、安在欽等並磔於西市，餘皆斬之。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished the captives and severed heads were paraded through the capital. Shouzhen's head was displayed at the southern market. His sons together with the rebel faction Sun Yuan, Liu Rui, Zhang Yansi, Liu Renyu, the monk Zonglun, Jing Yu, Zhang Qiu, Wang Tingxiu, Jiao Wenjie, An Zaiqin, and others were all dismembered at the western market; the rest were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished the captives and severed heads were paraded through the capital. Shouzhen's head was displayed at the southern market. His sons together with the rebel faction Sun Yuan, Liu Rui, Zhang Yansi, Liu Renyu, the monk Zonglun, Jing Yu, Zhang Qiu, Wang Tingxiu, Jiao Wenjie, An Zaiqin, and others were all dismembered at the western market; the rest were beheaded.

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：符後先適河中節度使李守貞之子崇訓。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu had first been married to Chongxun, son of Hezhong military governor Li Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu had first been married to Chongxun, son of Hezhong military governor Li Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 守貞嘗得術士，善聽聲，知人貴賤，守貞舉族悉令術士聽之，獨言後大富貴，當母儀天下。

translations.literal: Shouzhen once obtained a technician skilled at listening to voices and discerning noble and base. He had the entire clan listen; only Fu was said to be greatly wealthy and honored and destined to be mother of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen once obtained a technician skilled at listening to voices and discerning rank. He had the entire clan listen; only Fu was said to be destined for great wealth and honor and to become mother of the realm.

sentences.zh: 守貞信之，因曰：「吾婦尚為皇后，吾可知也。

translations.literal: Shouzhen believed it and therefore said: "If my daughter-in-law can become empress, I can imagine my own fate.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen believed it and therefore said, "If my daughter-in-law can become empress, I can guess my own fate.

sentences.zh: 」遂謀叛。
