translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，後獨免，周祖為世宗娶之，顯德中，冊為後。）〉

translations.literal: When the city fell, Fu alone was spared. The Zhou founder had her marry Shizong; in the Xiande era she was invested as empress.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Fu alone was spared. The Zhou founder had her marry Shizong, and in the Xiande era she was invested as empress.)〉

sentences.zh: 趙思綰，魏府人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Siwan was a man of Weifu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Siwan was a native of Weifu.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，趙在禮之據魏城也，思綰隸於帳下，累從之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang in Tang, when Zhao Zaili held Weicheng, Siwan served in his command and repeatedly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tongguang in Tang, when Zhao Zaili held Weicheng, Siwan served under his command and repeatedly followed him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 在禮卒，趙延壽籍其部曲，盡付於其子贊，思綰即其首領也。

translations.literal: When Zaili died, Zhao Yanshou registered his personal troops and entrusted them entirely to his son Zan; Siwan was their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaili died, Zhao Yanshou registered his personal troops and entrusted them entirely to his son Zan. Siwan was their leader.

sentences.zh: 高祖定河、洛，贊自河中移京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the He and Luo regions, Zan moved from Hezhong to Jingzhao Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu pacified the He and Luo regions, Zan moved from Hezhong to become governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 贊以久事契丹，常慮國家終不能容，乃與鳳翔侯益謀，引蜀兵為援，又令判官李恕入朝請覲，趙贊不待報赴闕，留思綰等數百人在京兆。

translations.literal: Zan, having long served the Khitan, always feared the state would never tolerate him. He therefore conspired with Fengxiang's Hou Yi to bring in Shu troops as reinforcements, and also had administrative aide Li Shu enter court to request an audience. Zhao Zan set out for court without waiting for a reply, leaving Siwan and several hundred men at Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, having long served the Khitan, always feared the state would never tolerate him. He conspired with Hou Yi of Fengxiang to bring in Shu troops as reinforcements and sent administrative aide Li Shu to court to request an audience. Zhao Zan set out for court without waiting for a reply, leaving Siwan and several hundred men at Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 會高祖遣王景崇等西赴鳳翔，行次京兆，時思綰等數百人在焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Gaozu sent Wang Jingchong and others west toward Fengxiang; as they halted at Jingzhao, Siwan and several hundred men were there.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Gaozu sent Wang Jingchong and others west toward Fengxiang. When they halted at Jingzhao, Siwan and several hundred men were there.

sentences.zh: 思綰等比是趙在禮禦士，本不刺面，景崇、齊藏珍既至京兆，欲令文面，以防逋逸。

translations.literal: Siwan and the others had been Zaili's personal guard in resisting the Khitan and had never had their faces tattooed. After Jingchong and Qi Cangzhen reached Jingzhao they wished to have their faces inscribed to prevent desertion.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan and the others had been Zhao Zaili's personal guard against the Khitan and had never had their faces tattooed. When Jingchong and Qi Cangzhen reached Jingzhao they wished to have their faces tattooed to prevent desertion.

sentences.zh: 景崇微露風旨，思綰厲聲先請自刺，以率其下，景崇壯之。

translations.literal: Jingchong slightly revealed his intent. Siwan loudly volunteered to tattoo himself first to lead his subordinates; Jingchong was impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong slightly revealed his intent. Siwan loudly volunteered to tattoo himself first to lead his men, and Jingchong was impressed.

sentences.zh: 藏珍竊言曰：「思綰粗暴難制，不如殺之。

translations.literal: Qi Cangzhen whispered: "Siwan is rough and hard to control—better kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Cangzhen whispered, "Siwan is rough and hard to control—better kill him.

sentences.zh: 」景崇不聽，但率之同赴鳳翔。

translations.literal: " Jingchong would not listen and only led them together toward Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingchong would not listen and led them together toward Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，遣供奉官王益部署思綰等赴闕。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this it sent Palace Attendant Wang Yi to escort Siwan and the others to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this it sent Palace Attendant Wang Yi to escort Siwan and the others to court.

sentences.zh: 思綰既發，行至途中，謂其黨常彥卿曰：「小太尉已入他手，吾輩至，則並死矣。

translations.literal: After Siwan set out and was on the road he said to his partisan Chang Yanqing: "The Little Grand Marshal has already fallen into others' hands. When we arrive, we shall all die together.
translations.idiomatic: After Siwan set out and was on the road he said to his partisan Chang Yanqing, "The Little Grand Marshal has already fallen into others' hands. When we arrive, we shall all die together.

sentences.zh: 」小太尉蓋謂趙贊也。

translations.literal: " "Little Grand Marshal" meant Zhao Zan.
translations.idiomatic: " "Little Grand Marshal" meant Zhao Zan.

sentences.zh: 彥卿曰：「臨機制變，子勿復言！

translations.literal: Yanqing said: "Seize the moment and change the plan—you need say no more!
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing said, "Seize the moment and change the plan—you need say no more!

sentences.zh: 」既行，至永興，副使安友規、巡檢使喬守溫出迎，於郊外離亭置酒。

translations.literal: " After they set out and reached Yongxing, Deputy Commissioner An Yougui and Inspection Commissioner Qiao Shouwen came out to welcome them and set out wine in a pavilion in the outer suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: " After they set out and reached Yongxing, Deputy Commissioner An Yougui and Inspection Commissioner Qiao Shouwen came out to welcome them and set out wine in a pavilion in the outer suburbs.

sentences.zh: 思綰前曰：「部下軍士已在城東安下，緣家屬在城，欲各將家今夜便宿城東。

translations.literal: Siwan stepped forward and said: "The soldiers under me have already encamped east of the city. Because their families are in the city, they wish each to bring his family tonight and lodge east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan stepped forward and said, "The soldiers under me have already encamped east of the city. Because their families are in the city, they wish each to bring his family tonight and lodge east of the city.

sentences.zh: 」守溫等然之。

translations.literal: " Shouwen and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouwen and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 思綰等辭去，與部下並無兵仗，才入西門，有州校坐門側，思綰遽奪其佩劍，即斬之。

translations.literal: Siwan and the others withdrew. They and their followers carried no weapons. Hardly had they entered the west gate when a prefectural officer sat beside the gate; Siwan suddenly seized his belt sword and at once beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan and the others withdrew. They and their followers carried no weapons. Hardly had they entered the west gate when a prefectural officer sat beside the gate. Siwan suddenly seized his belt sword and at once beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 其眾持白挺殺守門軍士十餘人，分眾守捉諸門。

translations.literal: His masses took white clubs and killed more than ten gate-guard soldiers, then divided forces to hold the various gates.
translations.idiomatic: His men took white clubs and killed more than ten gate-guard soldiers, then divided forces to hold the various gates.

sentences.zh: 思綰劫庫兵以授之，遂據其城，時乾祐元年三月二十四日也。

translations.literal: Siwan plundered the armory and distributed weapons, then seized the city. It was the twenty-fourth day of the third month in the first year of Qianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan plundered the armory and distributed weapons, then seized the city. It was the twenty-fourth day of the third month of Qianyou 1.

sentences.zh: 翌日，集城中丁壯得四千餘人，浚池隍，修樓櫓，旬浹之間，戰守皆備。

translations.literal: The next day they gathered the able-bodied men of the city and got more than four thousand. They dredged moats, repaired towers and ramparts; within ten days both offense and defense were ready.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they gathered more than four thousand able-bodied men of the city, dredged the moats, and repaired towers and ramparts. Within ten days both offense and defense were ready.

sentences.zh: 尋遣人送款於河中，李守貞遣使賫偽詔授思綰晉昌軍節度使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Presently they sent envoys to submit to Hezhong. Li Shouzhen sent envoys bearing a false edict appointing Siwan military governor of Jinchang and Honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Presently they sent envoys to submit to Hezhong. Li Shouzhen sent envoys bearing a false edict appointing Siwan military governor of Jinchang and Honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，命郭從義、王峻帥師伐之。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this it ordered Guo Congyi and Wang Jun to lead armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this it ordered Guo Congyi and Wang Jun to lead armies against him.

sentences.zh: 及攻其城，王師傷者甚眾，乃以長塹圍之。

translations.literal: When they attacked the city the imperial army suffered many wounded, and so they surrounded it with long trenches.
translations.idiomatic: When they attacked the city the imperial army suffered many wounded, and so they surrounded it with long trenches.

sentences.zh: 經年糧盡，遂殺人充食。

translations.literal: After a year grain ran out and they killed people to supplement food.
translations.idiomatic: After a year grain ran out and they killed people for food.

sentences.zh: 思綰嘗對眾取人膽以酒吞之，告眾曰：「吞此至一千，即膽氣無敵矣。」

translations.literal: Siwan once before the crowd took a human gall and swallowed it in wine, telling the crowd: "When I have swallowed a thousand of these, my gall-spirit will be without rival."
translations.idiomatic: Siwan once before the crowd took a human gall and swallowed it in wine, telling the crowd, "When I have swallowed a thousand of these, my courage will be without rival."

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《太平廣記》：賊臣趙思綰自倡亂至敗，凡食人肝六十六，無不面剖而膾之。）〉

translations.literal: (Extensive Records: The rebel minister Zhao Siwan, from the time he incited rebellion until defeat, ate sixty-six human livers in all, invariably slicing them from the face.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Extensive Records records that the rebel minister Zhao Siwan, from the time he incited rebellion until defeat, ate sixty-six human livers in all, invariably slicing them from the face.)〉

sentences.zh: 二年夏，食既盡，思綰計無從出，時左驍衛上將軍致仕李肅寓居城中，因與判官程讓能同言於思綰曰：「太尉比與國家無嫌，但負罪懼誅，遂為急計。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year food was exhausted. Siwan could think of no way out. At that time Left Xiaowei Palace Guard General Retired Li Su was living quietly in the city. He therefore spoke together with administrative aide Cheng Rangneng to Siwan, saying: "Grand Marshal, you have had no quarrel with the state until now—you only feared execution for your crime and so took desperate measures.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year food was exhausted and Siwan could think of no way out. Retired Left Xiaowei Palace Guard General Li Su was then living quietly in the city. He spoke together with administrative aide Cheng Rangneng to Siwan, saying, "Grand Marshal, you have had no quarrel with the state until now—you only feared execution for your crime and so took desperate measures.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷三處用兵，一城未下，太尉若翻然效順，率先歸命，以功補過，庶幾無患。

translations.literal: Now the court is fighting on three fronts and has not taken a single city. If Grand Marshal suddenly turns and submits, taking the lead in returning to allegiance, using merit to offset fault, you may yet escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court is fighting on three fronts and has not taken a single city. If Grand Marshal suddenly turns and submits, taking the lead in returning to allegiance and using merit to offset fault, you may yet escape harm.

sentences.zh: 若坐守窮城，端然待斃，則何貴於智也。」

translations.literal: If you sit holding a hopeless city, calmly awaiting death—where then is the value of wisdom?"
translations.idiomatic: If you sit holding a hopeless city, calmly awaiting death—where then is the value of wisdom?"

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》：思綰主藍田副鎮，有罪已發。

translations.literal: (Records of Old Affairs among the Gentry of Luoyang says: Siwan was in charge of the sub-garrison at Lantian; his crime had already come to light.
translations.idiomatic: (Records of Old Affairs among the Gentry of Luoyang records that Siwan commanded the sub-garrison at Lantian and his crime had already come to light.

sentences.zh: 李公肅時為環衛將兼雍耀三白渠使、雍耀莊宅使、節度副使，權軍府事，護而脫之，來謝於李公。

translations.literal: At that time Li Gongsu was a guard general and concurrently commissioner of the Three White Canals of Yong and Yao, commissioner of the Yong and Yao estates, and deputy military governor, holding authority over military headquarters affairs; he shielded and freed him, and Siwan came to thank Minister Li.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongsu was then a guard general and concurrently commissioner of the Three White Canals of Yong and Yao, commissioner of the Yong and Yao estates, and deputy military governor in charge of headquarters affairs. He shielded Siwan and secured his release, and Siwan came to thank him.

sentences.zh: 公歸宅，張夫人詰之曰：「趙思綰庸賤人，公何以免其禍？

translations.literal: When the minister returned home, Lady Zhang questioned him, saying: "Zhao Siwan is a base and worthless man—why did you spare him from punishment?
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home, Lady Zhang questioned him. "Zhao Siwan is a base and worthless man," she said. "Why did you spare him from punishment?

sentences.zh: 又何必見之乎？

translations.literal: Why must you even receive him?
translations.idiomatic: Why must you even receive him?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「某比不言，夫人問，須言之。

translations.literal: " He said: "I would not have spoken of this before, but since my lady asks, I must speak.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I would not have spoken of this before, but since you ask, I must tell you.

sentences.zh: 思綰者雖賤類，審觀其狀貌，真亂臣賊子，恨位下未有朕跡，不然，除去之，可也。

translations.literal: Although Siwan is of low birth, on careful observation of his bearing and appearance he is truly a rebellious minister and traitorous son; I regret that his rank is low and he has not yet shown signs of rebellion—otherwise he could have been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan may be of low birth, but a close look at his bearing shows a true rebel and traitor. I regret only that his rank is low and he has not yet shown open signs of rebellion—otherwise he could have been removed.

sentences.zh: 」夫人曰：「既不能除去，何妨以小惠啖之，無使銜怨。

translations.literal: " The lady said: "If he cannot be removed, why not win him with a small favor so that he bears no grudge?
translations.idiomatic: " His wife said, "If he cannot be removed, why not win him with a small favor so he bears no grudge?

sentences.zh: 」自後夫人密遣人令思綰之妻來參，夫人厚以衣物賜之，前後與錢物甚多。

translations.literal: " Thereafter the lady secretly sent people to have Siwan's wife come to pay respects; the lady generously bestowed clothing on her and gave her much money and goods before and after.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Lady Zhang secretly had Siwan's wife come to call on her and gave her generous gifts of clothing and much money and goods over time.

sentences.zh: 及漢朝，公以上將軍告老歸雍。

translations.literal: When the Han dynasty was established, the minister retired on account of age as a senior general and returned to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty was established, he retired as a senior general and returned to Yong.

sentences.zh: 未久，思綰過雍，遂閉門據雍城叛，衣冠之族，遭塗炭者眾，公全家免禍。

translations.literal: Before long Siwan passed through Yong, then shut the gates, seized Yong city, and rebelled. Many families of the gentry suffered ruin, but the minister's whole household escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Siwan passed through Yong, shut the gates, seized the city, and rebelled. Many gentry families were ruined, but the minister's entire household escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 終以計勸思綰納款，遂拔雍城。）〉

translations.literal: In the end he persuaded Siwan by stratagem to submit, and thus Yong city was taken.)
translations.idiomatic: In the end he persuaded Siwan by stratagem to submit, and thus Yong city was taken.)

sentences.zh: 思綰然之，即令讓能為章表，遣牙將劉成琦入朝。

translations.literal: Siwan agreed; he at once had Rangneng draft a memorial and sent military adjutant Liu Chengqi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan agreed. He had Rangneng draft a memorial at once and sent military adjutant Liu Chengqi to court.

sentences.zh: 制授思綰華州留後、檢校太保，以常彥卿為虢州刺史，遣內臣賫官告國信賜之。

translations.literal: By imperial order Siwan was made acting governor of Huazhou and Honorary Defender Grand Mentor; Chang Yanqing was made prefect of Guozhou; and an inner court official was sent bearing the commission and imperial letter of credence to bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Siwan was made acting governor of Huazhou and Honorary Defender Grand Mentor, Chang Yanqing was made prefect of Guozhou, and an inner court official was sent with the commission and imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 既受命，遲留未發。

translations.literal: After accepting the appointment he delayed and did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the appointment he lingered and did not depart.

sentences.zh: 郭從義、王峻等籌之曰：「狼子野心，終不可用，留之必貽後悔耳！

translations.literal: Guo Congyi, Wang Jun, and others deliberated and said: "A wolf cub has the heart of a wolf—he can never be used; if we leave him we are sure to regret it!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi, Wang Jun, and others deliberated and said, "A wolf cub will always have the heart of a wolf—he can never be trusted. If we leave him alive we are sure to regret it!

sentences.zh: 」既而從義、王峻等緩轡入城，陳列步騎至牙署，遣人召思綰曰：「太保登途，不暇出祖，對飲一杯，便申仳別。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward Congyi, Wang Jun, and the others entered the city at an easy pace, arrayed infantry and cavalry before the headquarters, and sent someone to summon Siwan, saying: "Grand Mentor is on the road and has no time for a full farewell banquet—let us share one cup face to face and then part.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward Congyi and Wang Jun entered the city at an easy pace, drew up infantry and cavalry before headquarters, and sent for Siwan, saying, "Grand Mentor is on the road and has no time for a full farewell—let us share one cup face to face and then part.

sentences.zh: 」思綰至，則執之，遂斬於市，並族其家。

translations.literal: " When Siwan arrived they seized him, then executed him in the market and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: " When Siwan arrived they seized him, executed him in the market, and exterminated his clan.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·郭從義傳》云：思綰困甚，從義遣人誘之，佯許以華州節鉞。

translations.literal: (Outline History of the Eastern Capital, biography of Guo Congyi, says: Siwan was in desperate straits; Congyi sent men to entice him and falsely promised him the military governorship of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: (Outline History of the Eastern Capital, biography of Guo Congyi, records that Siwan was in desperate straits. Congyi sent men to entice him and falsely promised him the military governorship of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 思綰信之，遂開門送款，從義入城，思綰謁見，即遣武士執之。）〉

translations.literal: Siwan believed it, then opened the gates and offered submission. Congyi entered the city; when Siwan came to audience he at once sent warriors to seize him.)
translations.idiomatic: Siwan believed it, opened the gates, and offered submission. Congyi entered the city, and when Siwan came to audience he at once sent warriors to seize him.)

sentences.zh: 思綰臨刑，市人爭投瓦石以擊之，軍吏不能禁。

translations.literal: As Siwan faced execution, people in the market vied to throw tiles and stones at him; military officers could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: As Siwan faced execution, townspeople vied to hurl tiles and stones at him, and the guards could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 是日，並部下叛黨新授虢州刺史常彥卿等五百餘人並誅之。

translations.literal: That same day, together with more than five hundred of his subordinates and fellow rebels, including the newly appointed Guozhou prefect Chang Yanqing, all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day more than five hundred of his subordinates and fellow rebels, including the newly appointed Guozhou prefect Chang Yanqing, were executed with him.

sentences.zh: 籍思綰家財，得二十餘萬貫，入於官。

translations.literal: Siwan's family property was inventoried and more than two hundred thousand strings of cash were obtained and entered into the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan's family property was inventoried: more than two hundred thousand strings of cash were seized for the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 始思綰入城，丁口僅十餘萬，及開城，惟餘萬人而已，其餓殍之數可知矣。

translations.literal: When Siwan first entered the city the registered population was barely a hundred thousand; when the city was opened only about ten thousand remained—the number who had starved to death can be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: When Siwan first seized the city the registered population was barely a hundred thousand. When the gates were opened only about ten thousand remained—the toll of starvation can be imagined.
